current.text: Rookie. Utah took him with the No. 2 pick in the 2026 draft.
Leaf calls him the best player in the draft class and the Jazz franchise player.
Most notes project him as a starter next to Keyonte George, Lauri Markkanen, Jaren Jackson Jr. and Jusuf Nurkic. One September note says he may not start.
He may play in short staggered stints, like Markkanen does.
He shares the ball with Markkanen, George and Jackson Jr., so he will get much less usage than in college or Summer League.
In Summer League he averaged 20 points, 5 assists and 5 turnovers on 38% usage. He shot under 40% from the field and 78% from the line. His games swung between explosive and bad.
Expect poor percentages and turnover problems early, as with most rookie guards. He should improve as the season goes on.
His assists this season are uncertain. Experts do not expect six assists right away.
Experts call an ADP of about 92 to 98 too high and see almost no chance he returns top 100 value. They find him fine as a late pick, around 110 to 134.
One expert gives him the tightest range in round 10: best case 76th, worst case about 148th. He would take him over AJ Dybantsa in any format.
Among rookies, one expert ranks him second in category leagues and third in points leagues. He could reach first if his assists develop.
If his game comes together, he is probably a top-15 fantasy player.
Experts expect Utah to try to win, with about 43 wins projected. They see no real risk of tanking or late-season shutdowns.

durable.text: At Kansas he had a 30% usage rate, huge three-point volume and strong scoring. His steals and blocks were strong for his position.
His assist numbers at Kansas were poor, though he was a good passer in high school.
One expert rates him as an electric shooter, near the top of his draft class.
He had injury problems in college, missing games and playing lower minutes.
Lloyd sees some athletic limitations at times.
He relies on volume scoring, which makes him better in points leagues than in category leagues.

note: The market (Yahoo rank 114 at 4.7 USD, ESPN rank 126 at 2.2 USD) matches the experts' call of a late pick around 110 to 130, so he is fine for 2 to 5 USD as a bench upside piece and not worth more. His rookie projection is about average in every category with no category clearly weak, so he fits any build without carrying one, but expect poor FG% and turnovers early. Early in the season, check whether he starts and how many minutes he gets next to George, Markkanen and Jackson Jr. Also watch whether his shooting and assists improve as the experts expect.
